why:
The fixture has no vector index, so this is the arm every server hits first and the one whose flag matters most. A server that answered without `degraded` here would be claiming a vector space it does not have. `degraded_reason` must say `no_index` and not `no_vector_support` even on a build with no vector support at all: the corpus is missing the artefact, which is the repair either way, and pinning the nearer cause is what keeps this case answerable identically by every build of every server.

`id` IS IN THE FIELD LIST AS OF #425, and it was not before — this case froze the shape of a retrieved result and omitted the one field a caller acts on. `retrieve` finds and `get_node` reads; the id is the handle between them, and a result carrying none is a result that cannot be followed. It was absent from the VECTOR arm and the omission here is why no case saw that.

This corpus has no index, so the vector arm remains unreachable from these cases and a second server implementing it is still ungraded on that half. That is a gap in the fixture, not in the contract: the shape is one shape, and a server whose two arms disagree about it is non-conforming whether or not a case here can reach both.

`truncated` JOINED THE FIELD LIST AT CONTRACT 0.22.0, AND ITS VALUE IS PINNED HERE. The key says whether a result's `text` is all of the text the index holds, and only a server querying a remote index that caps per-row storage can ever answer `true`. This fixture has no index at all, so the answer is `false` — and pinning the value rather than only the key is the point: a server that omits the field because it never truncates has left a caller unable to tell `whole` from `a server too old to say`, which is the same hole `degraded_reason` and `origin` were each widened to close.

`scope` AND `corpus` JOINED AT CONTRACT 0.24.0, AND BOTH ARE PINNED HERE BY VALUE. Several corpora may share one remote vector index, so a result has to be able to say which one it came from and a response has to say whether a span took effect. This fixture has no index of any kind, so the answers are `local` and null — and pinning them rather than only the keys is what catches the two ways a server gets this wrong without failing: reporting `across` because a span was ASKED for, and omitting `corpus` on the ground that it never has a foreign row to report.
